newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian smaller companies look good - Guinness Flight.
newsitem.headline: Asian smaller companies look good - Guinness Flight.

text.p: Global fund manager Guinness Flight Asia Ltd said on Monday that smaller companies in Asia would be the best play in the next market cycle as they offer good value investments.

In a statement, Guinness Flight chief investment officer Nerissa Lee said smaller companies -- those capitalised at less than US$500 million -- were often poorly researched and tended to have lower price/earnings ratios and higher earnings growth than blue chips.
"They are also more focused and provide a more direct access to Asia's growth," Lee said.
The smaller company sector was expanding rapidly, she said, adding that Asia's changing growth profile supports and favours the development.
With a pool of more than 2,740 smaller companies to choose from, Lee said there was ample scope to build and maintain a portfolio of excellent, high-growth and undervalued companies.
While Asian markets are off their highs, growth is likely to be sustained at high levels, she said.
"The markets are unlikely to get much cheaper and some, such as Hong Kong, have already turned up once more," Lee said.
